# Does NotebookLM have an API? The 2026 answer

October 18, 2026 · 5 min read

Yes and no, and the honest answer changed during 2026. Google does publish an API for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, in preview, behind a Cloud project and a licence. The consumer NotebookLM you log into with a personal Google account still has no developer key, and the standalone Podcast API that some posts point at is deprecated and not taking new customers.

Most answers you will find say flatly "there is no API". That was true and is now wrong, which is worse than either.

## What does the official API cover?​

Google documents a REST surface for Gemini Notebook Enterprise, including notebook operations and audio overviews — a notebook holds one audio overview at a time, created through `notebooks.audioOverviews.create`. It is marked pre-GA, which means the terms and the shape can both move.

The package is [`google.cloud.notebooklm.v1alpha`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rpc/google.cloud.notebooklm.v1alpha), served under Discovery Engine, and it holds exactly five services:

| Service | What it can do |
|---|---|
| `NotebookService` | create a notebook, get one, batch-delete, list recently viewed, share |
| `SourceService` | batch-create sources, batch-delete, get one |
| `AudioOverviewService` | create one audio overview, delete it — one per notebook at a time |
| `LabelService` | labels |
| `DiscoverSourcesService` | source discovery |

**Read that list for what is absent.** No method asks a notebook anything. There is no chat, no grounded answer, no citation — and no Studio output beyond audio: no report, no video, no infographic, no slide deck, no mind map, no flashcards, no quiz, no notes. The thing the product is *for* — answers grounded in your own sources, with the passage behind each claim — is not in its API. That single fact decides most people's choice, and almost no comparison states it.

The access path is the rest of the filter. It needs a Google Cloud project and a Gemini Enterprise or Education Premium licence, set up by an administrator, and calls are signed with the OAuth token of a user account holding that licence rather than with a service account. Third-party sources consistently report **$9 per licence per month with a 15-licence minimum** after a 30-day trial — figures worth checking against Google Cloud's own SKU list before you budget on them. Either way the smallest viable purchase is a team, not a developer. It is not a key you sign up for on a developer console, and it does not reach the notebooks in your personal account.

## What about the Podcast API?​

Deprecated. Google is not allowlisting new customers for it. If a tutorial tells you to request access, that tutorial is out of date.

## So what do people actually use?​

Community projects that drive the same interfaces the web app uses. There are several, in Python and in Node, exposing them as a CLI, as an MCP server, or as a local REST API. They work, they are fast, and they reach your own notebooks with your own login.

They also share one honest caveat: nothing about those interfaces is promised. Google can change them, and when it does the project breaks until someone fixes it. That has happened — the mid-2026 interface rebuild broke every such tool at once.

And they share the reason there is no consumer key to find. The consumer product authenticates with **a logged-in Google session**, which carries three properties worth knowing before you pick a tool: it is **bound to the machine** it was created on, so copied cookies are refused even while their local expiry still looks valid; it **expires server-side** while those cookies look fine, so the only reliable check is to navigate and see where you land; and an unpatched automated browser **gets flagged**. Any tool that hides those three from you has not solved them. The four projects that exist, measured side by side, are in [Gemini Notebook MCP servers compared](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/blog/gemini-notebook-mcp-servers-compared).

## Which should you pick?​

Three questions settle it.

**Do you have an enterprise licence and an administrator?** Then use the official API. It is supported, it is the only route with a contract behind it, and nothing below competes with that.

**Do you need your own personal notebooks?** Then the official API is out, and a community tool is the only route that exists.

**Do you need it to keep working unattended?** Weigh how quickly the project you pick has recovered from past breakages. That is the only signal that matters, and the commit history tells you more than the README.

## When is a community tool the wrong answer?​

- When the work is contractual — a client deliverable, a regulated pipeline, an SLA. An undocumented interface has no promise attached to it.
- When you only need text generation over documents. The Gemini API is public, supported and cheaper to reason about; NotebookLM's value is its grounding and citation behaviour, not its text generation.
- When you cannot run a browser anywhere. Login still happens in a real Chrome, once, even for the tools that avoid the browser afterwards.

## Trying this one​

Our own route is both an MCP server and a local REST API, so an agent and a workflow tool can use the same install.

```
# Claude Code
/plugin marketplace add roomi-fields/claude-plugins
/plugin install notebooklm@roomi-fields

# Then log into Google once, in a terminal
npx -y -p @roomi-fields/notebooklm-mcp notebooklm-mcp-setup-auth
```

Node 22 or newer. The REST route is in [the install guide](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/install), and the full endpoint list is in [the API reference](https://notebooklm.roomi-fields.com/notebooklm-rest-api).
